title: The boy who wouldn’t let go

card.keepWhy: He was told sixteen was the end. It wasn’t.
sources: Shaiva Puranic tradition (Shiva and Linga Puranas, and Tamil Shaiva temple tradition): the sage Mrikandu and his wife are granted a son, Markandeya, destined to live sixteen years; on his sixteenth birthday Yama comes; the boy embraces the linga; Yama’s noose falls on it; Shiva emerges and drives Yama back
Kalantaka, “the ender of Kala (time, death),” a name of Shiva from this story (the film’s note)
linga, the rounded stone form in which Shiva is worshipped in temples
check: The film’s note names the Markandeya Purana; most scholars place this rescue story in the Shiva, Linga and other Puranas rather than the Markandeya Purana itself. Confirm the source line.
“Stayed sixteen forever” (from the film); tellings differ, some say he was granted long or endless life. Confirm acceptable.
Today names the Mahamrityunjaya mantra (Rig Veda 7.59.12), which popular tradition links with Markandeya; the lesson doesn’t claim the link. Confirm it fits.

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? ever been told something is just your fate? “that’s how our family is.” “you’ll never be good at this.”
options: then this boy is your hero. listen.
then listen to how this one ends.
good. keep this one for someone who has.

steps.line: A wise sage and his wife were blessed with a son, Markandeya. But they were told his life would be short: just sixteen years.
The boy grew up kind, and devoted to Shiva.
On his sixteenth birthday, Yama arrived to take him: the god who ends each life’s journey.

steps.q: Yama has come for him. Markandeya grabs hold of something in the temple, and won’t let go. What?
steps.why: He threw his arms around the linga. At Thirukkadaiyur in Tamil Nadu, where many place the story, couples still come to mark their sixtieth birthdays and pray for long life.

steps.line: Markandeya ran to the temple, wrapped his arms around Shiva’s stone, the linga, and wouldn’t let go.

steps.q: Before he was born, many tellings say his parents were offered a choice. What did they choose?
o: A wise son with a short life
A long life for an ordinary son
No son, to spare them the grief
steps.why: A long life for a son of little worth, or sixteen years for a wise, devoted one. They chose the short, bright life.

steps.q: Yama throws his rope anyway, and it catches the stone too. What do you think happens?
o: Yama turns back on his own
Shiva bursts out of the stone
steps.why: Shiva bursts out of the stone itself. The boy never let go, and the one he held on to came to him.

steps.line: Yama cast his rope anyway, and it caught the linga too. Shiva burst out of the stone, and sent Yama away.
And Markandeya, the story says, stayed sixteen forever. Fate wasn’t the final word.
steps.label: today

steps.q: Yama’s rope caught the linga too. Why might that be the moment Shiva acts?
o: Markandeya finally cried out for help
Sixteen years had just run out
Yama had thrown his rope on Shiva himself
steps.why: Reaching for the linga was reaching for Shiva. In many tellings that was the line Yama shouldn’t have crossed, and Shiva kicked him away.

steps.q: Markandeya stayed sixteen forever. Tradition counts him among the chiranjivis. What are they?
o: Boys who were made into gods
Ones who live on, age after age
steps.why: Chiranjivi means long-lived; the lists include Hanuman and Vyasa. Some stories say Markandeya even lived through the great flood, and saw the child Vishnu on a banyan leaf.

say: here’s what i love. markandeya was told sixteen was the end. it wasn’t.
for many hindus, this story says fate isn’t always the final word. holding on to god with your whole heart can change an ending everyone thought was fixed.

steps.q: In this story Shiva is called Kalantaka. Kala can mean time, and death. What do you think Kalantaka means?
steps.why: Kalantaka: the one who ends death itself. That’s who Markandeya was holding on to.

today.say: pick one “that’s just my fate” belief about yourself, and write down one way it might not be true. many hindus chant the mahamrityunjaya mantra to shiva for courage in hard times. you can listen to it, learn it, or join in. it’s your choice.
options: then hold on to the other way. markandeya did.
that’s honest. one way it might not be is enough for today.
